Case :- Writ - C No. - 42495 of 2023
Petitioner :- Mahendra Pratap Pandey

Respondent :- National Highway Authority Of India And 2 Others
Counsel for Petitioner :- Deepak Kumar Vishwakarma,Vishwanath Vishwakarma

Counsel for Respondent :- C.S.C.,Rajesh Kumar Jaiswal
Hon'ble Manoj Kumar Gupta,Acting Chief Justice
Hon'ble Kshitij Shailendra,J.
1.

The instant petition has been filed praying for a writ of mandamus directing respondent no.3 to decide his application/ representation dated 17.05.2018 in relation to claim made by him for payment of compensation on account of acquisition of Arazi No.61 (Gha), area 0.0100 hectare,
situated at Mauja Rahimpur alias Muslimpur, Pargana and Tehsil Saidpur, District Ghazipur.
2. It is not disputed that the aforesaid land of the petitioner was acquired under the provisions of the National Highways Act, 1956 and award was declared on 30.01.2017.

sentences.text: The case of the petitioner is that the respondents have not assessed the value of super-structure standing over the acquired land while making award.
He, therefore, filed representation dated 17.05.2018 and when it was not decided, the instant petition has been filed.
4. In the counter affidavit filed by N.H.A.I. the stand taken is that no construction belonging to the petitioner was found to be in existence over the acquired land.
Moreover, the petitioner has remedy of challenging the award of the competent authority as per the provisions of Section 3-G(5) of the Act.
5. We find considerable force in the stand taken by the respondent no.1.
In case the petitioner was not satisfied with the award, he had the remedy of challenging the same by seeking arbitration under Section 3-G(5) of the Act.
6. Consequently, no ground is made out to entertain the claim in exercise of writ jurisdiction.
7. We, therefore, dispose of the instant petition with liberty to the petitioner to avail such other remedy as may be available.

Order Date :- 12.1.2024 AKShukla/-
(Kshitij Shailendra, J.) (Manoj Kumar Gupta, A.C.J.)
